NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI semiconductor value chain as a fabless chip designer, critically dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge wafer fabrication and SK Hynix for HBM memory, while commanding enormous pricing power over hyperscaler downstream customers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) who are locked into NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem for AI training and inference workloads. Its position is uniquely leveraged: upstream concentration risk is high given TSMC dependency, but downstream demand from cloud and AI spending far exceeds supply, giving NVIDIA exceptional revenue visibility and gross margins above 70%.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a 'fabless' designer of proprietary silicon and systems integrator that sources advanced components — displays, memory, modems, and chips — from a concentrated set of Asian and global technology suppliers. On the downstream side, Apple sells directly to consumers via its retail and online channels while also relying on carrier partners for iPhone distribution and platform giants like Google for high-margin Services revenue, making it both a hardware product company and a powerful platform intermediary.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the critical nexus of the global semiconductor supply chain as the world's dominant pure-play foundry, converting highly specialized equipment and materials from a concentrated set of suppliers into finished wafers for nearly every major fabless chip designer. Its upstream dependence on a small number of equipment makers—most notably ASML for irreplaceable EUV technology—and its downstream concentration among a handful of mega-cap technology customers (particularly Apple and NVIDIA) make TSMC both the essential backbone and a key single point of failure for the global electronics industry.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the core of the global memory supply chain as one of only three major producers of DRAM (alongside Samsung and SK Hynix) and a leading NAND flash manufacturer, making it heavily dependent on a concentrated set of capital equipment suppliers for its advanced fab processes. Its downstream customer base spans hyperscale cloud providers, AI accelerator manufacturers, mobile OEMs, and enterprise hardware vendors, with surging demand for High Bandwidth Memory from AI GPU customers like NVIDIA emerging as a pivotal growth driver.
